plans.text: Jobava: Bf4, e3, Bd3, Qf3 or Qd2 and castle long; Nb5 hits c7 whenever …a6 is missing. If Black castles short, g4–h4–h5 with the rooks on the g- and h-files.
Against …c5, Bortnyk plays e4 at once: the centre opens on his terms before …cxd4 and …a6 can happen. Develop quickly (Bb5+, Nf3, O-O-O or O-O) and use the lead.
Against …Bf5: f3, g4 and h4 hunt the bishop and gain kingside space; e3, Qd2 and O-O-O follow.
French by transposition: e4–e5 closes the centre; then f4, Nf3, and a kingside attack with Qg4 or the f-pawn.
Vienna Gambit: after fxe5 the e5-pawn cramps Black; Nf3, d3 or Qe2 to challenge the e4-knight, then castle and use the f-file.
Vienna without King's Gambit: Bc4, d3, Nf3 or Nge2, castle, and only then f4 — after …exf4, Bxf4 is a free developing move. Attack on the f-file.
Grand Prix: f4, Nf3, Bb5 or Bc4, O-O, d3, then Qe1–h4 and f5. All White's pieces go to the kingside.
150 Attack: Be3, Qd2, f3, Bh6 to trade the g7-bishop, O-O-O and h4–h5. Open the h-file against the castled king.
After 1…Nf6 2.e4: take space and develop (Nf3, Bc4 or d4), castle and aim the pieces at the kingside.
